dedupe_keys.name: quantum bit retransmission using universal quantum copying machine

description: Napoli, Antonio and colleagues document this resource in the B5G-OPEN community. The authors state that they developed a simulation platform to evaluate quantum automatic repeat request. QARQ uses imperfect clones generated through a Universal Quantum Copying Machine and is inspired by classical ARQ reliability protocols. Coverage is a numerical feasibility experiment for quantum communications. Reported suitability is limited to applications that tolerate low fidelity; perfect cloning is not claimed. The platform exists according to the source, but its name beyond QARQ, programming language, interfaces and public code availability are unspecified. Zenodo provides the descriptive publication with open access; its stated licence is cc-by-4.0. Its publication licence does not establish a code licence or source-code availability. A limitation is that the native metadata do not establish all implementation settings, uncertainty bounds or independent reproducibility. Only descriptive metadata were inspected. Related records and companion papers retain their source-defined roles; they do not imply independent measurements.
